text:
Erin L: kicking off GPU region bring-up QA for edge-fleet (lon2). want to run through a concise checklist and handoff plan. I put the health gates below.

Mike C: 👍 list please. aiming for canary tomorrow morning (UTC).

Erin L: top-level gates: 1) infra provisioning OK (k8s nodes, volumes, networking) 2) GPU capacity validated + MIG profiles 3) kernel/driver sanity (nvidia + cudnn) 4) SLO smoke (p50/p95 gen lat, token/sec) 5) network path checks between control-plane and GPUs 6) cost/capacity knobs validated (burst/spot behavior) 7) clear handoff checklist for support oncall.

Jess P: can we include KV/prefix cache warmup and verification? last time cold cache spiked latency.

Erin L: added. also verify automatic prefix caching is enabled on canary routes and that hit-rate >= 70% after warmup.

Raj S: for GPU capacity I'm going to run a scaled token-gen test across H100 pools with the following riff:
```
# quick load test harness
./loadgen --model riv-7b --seq 1024 --concurrency 40 --duration 300
```
Expect to see steady tokens/s across nodes and no OOM. Will also check NVLink health and GPU temps.

Mike C: for MIG/partitioning: confirm node has expected MIG slices and driver exposes them: `nvidia-smi mig -lgi` and `docker run --gpus all nvidia/cuda:11.8-base nvidia-smi`

Jess P: network checks: verify MTU end-to-end (no fragmentation), test jumbo frames if used, and run a short iperf3 between control-plane and worker racked hosts. watch for packet loss > 0.1%.

Erin L: add explicit test for leaf-spine latency: traceroute + ping sweep to rule out asymmetric routing on the new fabric. also confirm route table entries for subnets are pinned to expected AZs (avoid cross-AZ egress charges).

Raj S: SLO numbers proposed for this bring-up (canary target):
- gen p50 < 60ms (short prompts <=64 tokens)
- gen p95 < 220ms
- sustained throughput >= 10000 tokens/s per 10-node pool for 1m windows
- error rate (5xx) < 0.2%

Mike C: cost guardrails: set burst budget to 2x baseline for first 6 hours then drop to normal. enable autoscale cap to avoid runaway spot replacements. set billing alert at $/hour threshold for the fleet.

Jess P: ops validation snippet I ran earlier (returns empty if all healthy):
```
kubectl get pods -n redwood-inference -o wide | grep -v Running
kubectl top nodes --selector=pool=lon2-gpu
```
Result: nothing abnormal in dev cluster; will run again against canary.

infra-bot: deploy-check: canary deployment created (canary-2026-03-18), 2/2 services ready, rollout 10% traffic -> 90% fallback.

Erin L: handoff notes for SRE oncall: 1) escalation path (pager + slack) 2) exact runbook link (https://internal.redwood/ops/bringup/lon2) 3) temporary mitigation toggles (route to fallback model, reduce concurrency, disable prefix cache) 4) cost kill switch (terminate burst ASG).

Mike C: risk items: spot preemption pattern in this region historically high between 0300-0500 UTC, recommend avoid scheduled heavy runs then. Also check local pricing is within 10% of forecast; adjust committed capacity if not.

Jess P: final pre-canary checklist (quick):
- [x] k8s nodes provisioned with GPUs attached
- [x] storage PVs available and IO perf validated (fio 1000MB rw mixed)
- [x] nvidia driver + cuda verified on all nodes
- [x] network MTU/latency/packet-loss under thresholds
- [x] KV/prefix cache warmup plan documented
- [x] canary deploy created and infra-bot confirms 10% traffic
- [ ] run full loadgen for 30m and confirm SLOs

Erin L: I'll run the 30m loadgen at 08:00 UTC, ping if you want to watch metrics. if it looks good, we do 50% traffic shift and then handoff to oncall to monitor for 2 hours.

Raj S: will capture logs/summaries and post back here after run (noting any OOMs, nvlink errs, or driver hangs).

Mike C: thanks team. tagging @oncall-sre for awareness. :thumbsup:

Erin L: thanks — keeping this thread as the single source for canary notes. once we pass handoff I'll close and attach the postmortem checklist.
